issues.description: Class de.tum.in.ase.eist.rest.PersonResource: constructor parameter type differs between artifacts. The template declares a constructor public PersonResource(PersonService personService) (PersonService injected and assigned to the final field). The solution declares public PersonResource(de.tum.in.ase.eist.service.NoteService noteService) and sets this.personService = null. This type/signature mismatch causes the PersonResource in the solution to have a null personService (runtime failures) and does not match the expected dependency-injection of PersonService described in the problem statement.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the solution's PersonResource constructor to accept a PersonService and assign it to the field. For example: public PersonResource(PersonService personService) { this.personService = personService; } Ensure dependency injection binds a PersonService so controller methods can call personService without causing null-pointer errors.

issues.description: Constructor parameter identifier and type in solution's PersonResource differ from the template expectation. The template uses parameter name personService of type PersonService and assigns it to the field this.personService. The solution uses a parameter named noteService of type de.tum.in.ase.eist.service.NoteService and then sets this.personService = null. The mismatched parameter name and type make the constructor implementation semantically incorrect and confusing for students reading the example.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename and retarget the solution constructor parameter to match the conceptual service injected: use PersonService personService and assign it (this.personService = personService). Remove the incorrect NoteService parameter and the explicit null assignment so the constructor consistently reflects the intended dependency injection.
